source.highlight: The true fake story behind the annual Virginia City Camel Race
source.after: Back in the 1950s, a newspaper editor in Nevada wrote a fake story about a camel race happening in his town as a joke. Eventually, he helped make it a real thing and the annual Virginia City Camel Race was born, which continues to this day. … Bob Richards lied the thing right into existence.

source.before: It was the 50th time that the race has run through all five boroughs of the city.
source.highlight: There were just over 2,000 competitors in 1976, the seventh running of the race, including only 88 women. About 60,000 runners stepped up to the starting line Sunday, with nearly half of them women.
source.after: There were runners from more than 140 countries competing Sunday, including defending men's Kipruto.

source.highlight: FALKNER: The question is not whether you can be a professional athlete by watching the NFL, but are you better at football for watching sports than if you had never watched anything? And the answer is absolutely yes.
